diagnosis: EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
legend: A case of splenic involvement of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma in which the tumour is well demarcated from the surrounding splenic tissue by a fibrous pseudocapsule. There are numerous coalescent non-caseating epithelioid granulomas within the lesion (<<30602>>). The scattered spindle to ovoid tumour cells are found within a prominent lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate between the granulomas (<<30603>>). High magnification of scattered spindle to ovoid tumour cells (<<30614>>). The tumour cells express CD21 (<<30615>>). EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma involving the liver: synchronous involvement of the liver is present in the same case (<<30617>>), and larger atypical cells with more pronounced pleomorphism are evident (<<30621>>).

diagnosis: EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
legend: Tumour cells are highlighted by dual labelling using EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization (brown) and CD21 immunostaining (red).

diagnosis: EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma of adenoid
legend: The adenoid tumour shows a prominent inflammatory background with the presence of overlying xanthomatous cells.

diagnosis: EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma of adenoid
legend: Mononuclear and binucleated tumour cells with prominent nucleoli are dispersed within a rich lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, showing some resemblance to HRS cells.

diagnosis: EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma of spleen
legend: Spindle cells show a loose fascicular to storiform growth pattern and exhibit a range of nuclear atypia. The background is rich in lymphocytes and plasma cells (<<31150>>). The spindle cells show indistinct cell borders. The nuclei have thin nuclear membranes, vesicular chromatin, and distinct nucleoli. Binucleated cells are seen. Nuclear pleomorphism is relatively mild in this example. There are admixed lymphocytes and plasma cells (<<31151>>). On in situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER), both bland-looking and overtly atypical neoplastic spindle cells are highlighted (<<31153>>).

title: Comparison of the epidemiological and clinical features of EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma and follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
tablehtml:
Feature

EBV+ inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma

Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma

Epidemiology

Predominantly reported in Asian populations

No ethnic predilection

Sex

Female predilection

No sex predilection

Median age

55 years

50 years

Sites of disease

Predominantly spleen and liver; rarely colon (polyp), tonsils, bronchus, mesentery

Lymph node or practically any extranodal site, most commonly abdomen (including gastrointestinal tract, retroperitoneum) and upper aerodigestive tract (tonsil, nasopharynx, parapharynx)

Presentation

Most commonly presenting with splenomegaly or hepatomegaly; paraneoplastic pemphigus very rare

Lymphadenopathy or mass lesion attributable to extranodal disease; may be associated with autoimmune diseases, such as paraneoplastic pemphigus and myasthenia gravis

Constitutional symptoms

Present in a proportion of patients

Very rare

Predisposing conditions

Unknown

Hyaline-vascular Castleman disease in a proportion of cases

Histology

Dispersed tumour cells; many admixed lymphocytes and plasma cells

Compact spindly to oval tumour cells with indistinct cell borders; sprinkling of lymphocytes

Behaviour

Generally indolent; recurrence ~30%, distant metastasis uncommon

Variable; local recurrence 28–40%, distant metastasis > 25%

EBV association

Always present (by definition)

Extremely rare
